questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Describe the following structural features:

(i) Normal fault. (2 marks)

(ii) Syncline. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Normal fault:** a fracture in the rocks along which the rocks have moved, the **hanging wall (the block above the fault plane) moving DOWN relative to the footwall**. The fault plane is steep (about $60^\circ$ from the horizontal). It is produced by **tensional (pulling-apart) forces** and causes **lengthening (extension)** of the crust. Two parallel normal faults dipping towards each other produce a **graben (rift valley)**; dipping away from each other they leave a **horst**.

**(ii) Syncline:** a **downfold** of rock beds, in the shape of a trough or a U. The two limbs **dip towards the axis**, and the **youngest rocks lie in the centre (core)** of the fold, with older rocks outside. It is produced by **compressional forces**; it is the opposite of an anticline.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) (i) Define the term "Metamorphism". (2 marks)

(ii) Outline the common textures in metamorphic rocks. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Metamorphism** is the **change in the mineral composition, texture and structure of pre-existing rocks (igneous, sedimentary or older metamorphic) in the SOLID state**, caused by **heat, pressure and chemically active fluids**, without the rock melting.

**(ii) Common textures of metamorphic rocks:**

1. **Foliated texture:** minerals (micas, chlorite) are lined up in parallel layers or bands by directed pressure: **slaty cleavage** (slate), **schistosity** (schist) and **gneissic banding** (gneiss).
2. **Non-foliated (granular, crystalline) texture:** interlocking crystals of about equal size, with no alignment, as in **marble** and **quartzite** (also hornfels).
3. **Porphyroblastic texture:** large new crystals (e.g. garnet) set in a finer-grained matrix.

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) Define the term viscosity of magma. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown: **Viscosity of magma** is its **resistance to flow** (how thick or runny it is). A magma rich in silica and cooler is **viscous** (thick, flows slowly, as in rhyolitic magma); a hot magma poor in silica is **fluid** (runny, flows easily, as in basaltic magma).
